subject: Phasing, start date and credit structure for Dedicated capacity (ZenoTech)
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@zenotech.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@zenotech.com
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — term options and start window

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the call this morning. ZenoTech is excited about Redwood's Dedicated offering; a couple items we need to lock down before legal drafts an SOW:

- Term length: procurement prefers a 36-month reserved commit for price stability, but our finance team will only sign with a staged ramp and a later capacity start date to avoid upfront spend.
- Ramp schedule: propose 3 phases across quarters (25% -> 60% -> 100%) tied to model rollouts.
- Credits: we'd like an implementation credit to offset the first-month bill and a short period of waived overage charges during the ramp.

Can you share a formal counter that shows pricing at 12/24/36 months with an explicit phased-start option and the credits you can offer? Also include any constraints around start date (earliest vs latest) and the SLA/throughput guarantees tied to reserved commit.

Elena
Elena Rossi
Director of ML Platforms, ZenoTech
elena@zenotech.com
+44 20 7123 4567
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@zenotech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-11T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — term options and start window

Hi Elena — appreciate the clear summary. We're happy to model multiple term lengths and a phased-start. Before I put numbers in writing, quick clarifying Qs so we size the GPU pool and throughput guarantees correctly: 

1) Target steady-state QPS/token throughput at 90th pct for phase 3? (helps pick GPU class & kernel profile)
2) Expected percent of traffic that needs sub-100ms tail latency vs batch-tolerant work.
3) Do you require strict data residency in the EU region only?

Initial answers below on constraints and options:
- Start date: we can set an "activation window" up to 90 days after signature for no penalty; beyond that we’d need to revisit pricing if costs materially change.
- Phased-start: supported. We can define explicit capacity bands and billing floors per phase (e.g., pay for committed capacity in band, with small overage rates during ramp).
- Credits: for a 36-month commit we can offer a one-time implementation credit and two months of overage protection during the first phase. For 24-month we can offer a smaller credit and one month protection.

I'll run numbers with Karthik and Ben and send a counter with a simple table for 12/24/36 month pricing + ramp templates tomorrow.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Revenue — EMEA, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: FW: ZenoTech — pricing scenarios (need quick pricing grid)

Team — forwarding Elena's request. Need a short pricing grid for the three term options that reflects: GPU pool sizing (A100-40 vs A100-80 equivalents), committed vCPU/GPU ratio, guaranteed tokens/sec at 90th pct, and the credit structure. Key asks from Elena: staged ramp, activation window up to 90 days, and overage protection during phase 1.

Proposed quick approach (what to validate):
- 12mo: higher $/GPU, no implementation credit, 30-day activation window, 1 month overage protection at 50% cap.
- 24mo: mid $/GPU, $40k implementation credit, 60-day activation window, 1 month overage protection at 75% cap.
- 36mo: best $/GPU, $80k implementation credit, 90-day activation window, 2 months overage protection at 100% cap.

Also attaching the capacity matrix I mocked (zeno_capacity_matrix.csv) and a marked-up SOW. Thoughts? If you're aligned, I'll send the counter to Elena with the table and attachment references.

— Mina
(Attachment: zeno_capacity_matrix.csv, ZenoTech_SOW_draft_v2.pdf)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@zenotech.com>, procurement@zenotech.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T11:50:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood counter: term & phased-start proposal (table + attachments)

Elena — following up with a concise counterproposal attached. Key points summarized below (see attached SOW and capacity matrix for row-level detail):

Summary table (high level):
- 12-month: list price $/GPU-hour = $X; no implementation credit; activation window = 30 days; phase ramp floors = 40% / 70% / 100%; overage protection = 1 month at 50% cap.
- 24-month: list price = $Y (approx -12% vs 12mo); implementation credit = $40,000; activation window = 60 days; ramp floors = 25% / 60% / 100%; overage protection = 1 month at 75% cap.
- 36-month: list price = $Z (approx -22% vs 12mo); implementation credit = $80,000; activation window = 90 days; ramp floors = 20% / 55% / 100%; overage protection = 2 months at 100% cap.

Operational notes:
- Throughput guarantees are tied to the committed GPU pool size and per-route latency SLOs in the SOW. If ZenoTech requires strict sub-100ms tail latency for >30% of traffic, we recommend the A100-80-equivalent pool for phase 3 (will be reflected in the capacity matrix).
- We can include a clause that allows ZenoTech to delay activation beyond the activation window by mutual agreement without repricing for events tied to Force Majeure or documented regulatory restrictions.

Next steps / asks from your side:
1) Confirm which term you prefer (12/24/36) and whether the activation window is workable.
2) Confirm the target 90th pct throughput for phase 3 so we lock in the GPU class.
3) If legal wants redlines, please send them to procurement@redwood.com; we can turn SOW redlines within 48 hours.

Attachments: ZenoTech_SOW_draft_v2.pdf, zeno_capacity_matrix.csv

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the table.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Revenue — EMEA, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
From: Elena Rossi <elena@zenotech.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@zenotech.com
Date: 2026-09-15T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counter: term & phased-start proposal (table + attachments)

Mina — thanks for the clear table and the attachments. Quick responses:

- The team is comfortable moving forward on the 24-month plan with the $40k implementation credit and a 60-day activation window. That aligns best to our budgeting cycles.
- For phase 3 we want a target 90th pct tokens/sec equivalent to 1.8k QPS sustained (we'll send an internal dashboard snippet).
- Procurement would like the two-month overage protection clarified: in the 24-month row you listed 1 month at 75% cap — please confirm that overage protection applies to the first phase only and whether we can convert unused credit to a one-time invoice credit if not used.

If you can confirm those two items (overage protection scope + conversion of leftover credit), we will ask legal to start SOW review. Can you also confirm you're okay with an activation window of up to 60 days from signature?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Elena
Notes: Thread archived in Mina's Sales > Active Deals > ZenoTech folder.
